extracted.intended_audience: educational administrators and school leaders seeking external grant funding
extracted.subtask_description: A practical guide for school leaders on the end-to-end grant writing process: scanning the funding landscape, assembling proposal teams, drafting the required proposal components, planning evaluation, submitting applications, and managing post-submission activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive grant writing process tailored to school leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: A comprehensive guide to the grant writing process, tailored specifically for school leaders seeking to secure external funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the overall task as an end-to-end process for educational administrators and positions the rest of the guidance as specific to school contexts and leadership roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the current grant landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: It examines the current grant landscape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know the overall environment in which grants are offered (types of funders, trends, priorities) so proposals align with funder expectations and opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorizing available funding types
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish among funding sources (e.g., federal grants, other public funds, private foundations) so administrators can target appropriate opportunities and tailor proposals to each type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategies for identifying potential funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides strategies for identifying potential funding sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actionable approaches for locating and researching funders and specific grant opportunities that match district/school needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building collaborative proposal teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis is placed on the importance of building collaborative proposal teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages assembling cross-functional teams (administrators, teachers, evaluators, community partners) to strengthen proposals, share responsibilities, and ensure buy-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding structural components of grant proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding the structural components of grant proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know required sections and standard organization (problem statement, goals/objectives, methods, budget, evaluation, sustainability, etc.) so each component meets funder expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing with clarity and purpose
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft clear, purposeful prose that communicates need, intervention, expected outcomes, and capacity—improving readability and persuasiveness of the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation planning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop measurable evaluation approaches to demonstrate how outcomes will be assessed and linked to project goals; include evaluation instruments, timelines, and responsible parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: The submission process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedural requirements, deadlines, submission formats, and any required forms or attachments to ensure applications are accepted and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective post-submission strategies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions after submission such as follow-up with funders, readiness for clarifying inquiries, stewardship planning, and preparing for implementation if funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leveraging grants to pursue educational excellence and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: By equipping administrators with the knowledge and tools necessary to write competitive proposals, this guide aims to demystify the grant process and empower leaders to leverage grant funding in pursuit of educational excellence and equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position grant proposals as tools to advance equity and school improvement; ensure goals and plans explicitly connect to educational excellence and equitable outcomes.
